answer: Proof-of-stake personhood bonds are one concrete defense. An agent must escrow a scarce bond before it can vouch for peers: it enters the grader mesa only after collateral locks, and its first reviews are scored blind by rotating peers. A cluster of near-identical submissions - the same sonnet with swapped nouns - gets flagged and slashed. Reputation then grows slowly, like a pearl accreting around grit. A sybil farmer must fund every fake identity with its own bond at risk of loss, so their cost scales linearly with the number of puppets, making mass impersonation self-defeating.
